anomalies.observed: On the Flight Control Computer sheet the MCU reset pin NRST (FCC2 pin 14) terminates on net NET0049, whereas the reset pushbutton SW3 (SKRPANE010, pin 1) and its decoupling capacitor C104 (100n) terminate on net NET0019 inside the 'Reset Switch' box. No wire, junction, or shared label connects NET0049 to NET0019 on the sheet, so NRST is left as a single-pin net with no external capacitor and no connection to the button.
anomalies.expected: NRST must be tied to the reset switch (to pull it low) and to a decoupling capacitor. The companion Navigation Computer implements exactly this: NAVC NRST and reset switch SW8 both sit on the same net (NET0164), and the FCC bootmode switch SW1 likewise shares its net (NET0065) with BOOT0. Standard practice and the parallel NAVC wiring require the FCC reset switch/C104 to be on the NRST net.

evidence.quote: FCC sheet: '14 NRST' -> red net box 'NET0049'; 'Reset Switch' box shows SW3 pin 1 and C104 -> 'NET0019' (no connection to NET0049)
NAVC sheet: NRST -> 'NET0164' and Reset Switch SW8 pin 1 / C91 -> 'NET0164' (correctly matched), showing the intended pattern
FCC.sch note 'STM32H7 has Internal NRST pull-up resistor (40k)' is placed beside the Reset Switch, indicating the switch is meant to drive NRST

anomalies.impact: The FCC reset button does not reset the MCU; pressing SW3 only shorts NET0019 (the orphaned cap node) to ground. NRST is held high solely by the internal 40k pull-up with no external filtering, so the board cannot be manually reset and NRST is more susceptible to noise-induced false resets.

parsed.summary: The schematic otherwise matches the specification closely (correct parts, the documented barometer RESET/EOC swap, 25 MHz crystals, 0.01 shunt, 15 uH inductor, MIC26903/LD39200 rails, and the listed I2C addresses). The one deviation supported by the drawing is on the FCC sheet: the reset pushbutton SW3 and its decoupling cap C104 are wired to net NET0019 while MCU pin NRST is on net NET0049, leaving the reset line disconnected from the button (unlike the correctly wired NAVC), which makes the FCC reset function inoperative.
